text: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Slope limiters: minmod, Superbee, MC, van Leer, and van Albada Limiters trade linear high-order reconstruction for a nonlinear choice of local slope. Open the limiter notebook to compare five choices on identical grids and time integrators, together with first-order and unlimited scalar baselines. Reconstruction and the ratio convention# For uniform cells, let the backward and forward increments be ai=uˉi−uˉi−1,bi=uˉi+1−uˉi,ri=ai/bi,si=ϕ(ri)bi.ai​=uˉi​−uˉi−1​,bi​=uˉi+1​−uˉi​,ri​=ai​/bi​,si​=ϕ(ri​)bi​. The two states reconstructed from cell i are ui+1/2L=uˉi+12si,ui−1/2R=uˉi−12si.ui+1/2L​=uˉi​+21​si​,ui−1/2R​=uˉi​−21​si​. The implementation works directly with a and b, so a zero denominator at a plateau requires neither a numerical epsilon nor an arbitrary ratio. Opposite signs or either zero increment give zero limited slope. These are increments; divide by cell width only if a derivative is required. Five limiter functions# Each function below is zero for r ≤ 0. For r > 0: ϕminmod(r)=min⁡(1,r),ϕSuperbee(r)=max⁡{min⁡(2r,1),min⁡(r,2)},ϕMC(r)=min⁡{2r,(1+r)/2,2},ϕvan Leer(r)=2r/(1+r),ϕvan Albada(r)=(r2+r)/(r2+1).ϕminmod​(r)ϕSuperbee​(r)ϕMC​(r)ϕvan Leer​(r)ϕvan Albada​(r)​=min(1,r),=max{min(2r,1),min(r,2)},=min{2r,(1+r)/2,2},=2r/(1+r),=(r2+r)/(r2+1).​ This is the clipped, symmetric van Albada form, without an epsilon regularization; other variants differ near extrema. MC means monotonized central. All five satisfy phi(1)=1 and the plotted scalar bounds 0 ≤ phi(r) ≤ min(2r,2). See Sweby (1984) for the scalar flux-limiter framework and Roe's compressive construction, and the Clawpack limiter documentation and MPI-AMRVAC slope-limiter notes for implementation conventions. Names shared by different codes do not settle which variables, time integrator, or epsilon are used. Minmod chooses the smaller same-sign increment. Superbee takes a more compressive slope and can sharpen a smooth feature into a plateau. MC and van Leer retain more slope than minmod in many monotone regions. The notebook lets the error, variation, and overshoot measurements qualify those tendencies; no limiter wins every problem. Computed comparisons# The scalar equation is u_t + a u_x = 0 on [0,1], with periodic boundaries. All runs use conservative finite volumes, upwind interface fluxes, SSPRK(3,3), N=200, |a| dt/dx ≤ 0.3, and final time 1. The last step is shortened. Both directions a=±1 are computed. The two profiles are a unit square pulse on [0.2,0.4] and sin(2πx). Initial and reference values are exact cell averages, including partially covered square-pulse cells and the sine's sinc factor. Displayed L1 errors use those cell averages. Periodic total variation includes the last-to-first cell jump; mass is dx times the sum. Maximum TV uses every saved full-step diagnostic, including the initial state. The first-order comparison has zero slope. The unlimited comparison uses the centered slope (a+b)/2 with the same flux and SSPRK3; it can produce oscillations. It is not the Lax–Wendroff fully discrete method. The separate Sod comparison uses the existing ideal-gas setup, gamma=1.4, N=200, t=0.2, HLLC, primitive-variable reconstruction, and SSPRK3 at CFL=0.3. Only the slope choice changes. Its density error is pointwise, following the existing Sod convention; it is not an exact cell-average error. Outflow boundaries mean that the periodic scalar mass/TV diagnostics are not applied to this panel. Smooth sine refinement at N=40,80,160 and t=0.2 reports measured L1 errors and orders. A second-order label describes smooth-region consistency, not uniform pointwise accuracy at extrema or a second-order error on discontinuities. TVD is a property of the complete scalar update# For this scalar MUSCL operator, the stated slope bounds together with |a| dt/dx ≤ 1/2 give a TVD forward-Euler building block; SSPRK3 preserves its convex stability property under that bound. The executable solver restricts CFL to this range. Tests check both signs, periodic conservation, full-step variation, bounds, and a forward-Euler random-data case at CFL=1/2. The same function applied componentwise to Euler primitive variables is not a general system TVD theorem, entropy condition, or guarantee of positive cell averages. Characteristic reconstruction and a fully discrete positivity construction are separate extensions. See advanced limiters for TVB extrema relaxation and conservative positive-state scaling. Reproduce and inspect# python -m numart.cli run sod --method muscl --riemann hllc --limiter superbee --n 200 python scripts/build_limiters.py python scripts/sync_web_content.py from numart import get_problem, solve from numart.tvd import solve_advection sod = solve(get_problem("sod"), limiter="mc") pulse = solve_advection(profile="square", limiter="van-leer", speed=-1.) docs/figures/limiters.json records all plotted arrays, refinement results, diagnostics, and source hashes. The browser selects these Python-computed curves; it does not run another implementation of the PDE solver. Default MUSCL remains minmod.
